package.title: Tempo.Blazor.EmailTemplates.Abstractions
package.description: Logic and contracts for the Tempo.Blazor email template editor: block model, MJML generation and import, template/validation/preview contracts, variable extraction, DTOs and validators. No Blazor dependency, no Scriban/Mjml.Net/AngleSharp dependency (the local engine ships separately as Tempo.Blazor.EmailTemplates.Engine) – safe to reference from API/service projects and usable from Blazor WebAssembly.

items.description: AddTempoEmailTemplateModel — the model side of the email template editor: block registry, MJML and plain-text generators, the request validators with their closed JSON localizer, the conservative BCL HTML sanitizer, the regex variable extractor and the one shared TemplateSecurityOptions instance. Idempotent, and it never registers an engine type: no ITemplateEngine, IMjmlCompiler, ITemplateValidator, IEmailTemplateRenderer or IEmailPreviewRenderer. Add Tempo.Blazor.EmailTemplates.Engine (AddTempoEmailTemplateEngine) for the local pipeline, or supply a host IEmailPreviewRenderer / ITemplateValidator yourself.

Limits applied when a template enters the application: the size of the MJML input, the number of sections and blocks, and how deeply blocks may nest. They guard both the MJML importer and the JSON deserialization against a hostile or broken document (a "billion laughs" style tree, a runaway paste) and are reusable through EmailDocumentLimitsValidator before a document is saved.

members.name: MaxBlocks
members.description: Maximum number of blocks in the imported document, including blocks nested in hero, group and wrapper containers (default 2000). Exceeding it fails the import with TooManyBlocks.

members.name: MaxInputBytes
members.description: Maximum size of the input in UTF-8 bytes (not in characters), default 5 MB. Exceeding it fails the import with InputTooLarge instead of parsing the payload.

members.name: MaxNestingDepth
members.description: Maximum nesting depth of blocks (default 8). A block directly in a section column is depth 1 and every hero/group/wrapper level adds one — the same convention LayoutValidator uses. Exceeding it fails the import with TooDeeplyNested.

members.name: MaxSections
members.description: Maximum number of sections in the imported document, including sections nested inside a wrapper (default 200). Exceeding it fails the import with TooManySections.

Localization keys for import diagnostics.

members.name: BlockedLink
members.description: Any other block's link (button, image, navbar link, social element, carousel image, hero/wrapper/section background, mj-font) used a scheme outside the URL allow-list (§3.7a). Same contract as BlockedTableLink: the value survives for editing and every emission path fail-closes it to #. The message carries the refused SCHEME, never the URL.

members.name: BlockedTableLink
members.description: A table cell's link used a scheme outside the URL allow-list (§3.7a). The value is kept in the model so the editor can show and fix it; every emission path (generator, text version, renderer) fail-closes it.

members.name: DroppedAttribute
members.description: An imported attribute was dropped because the pipeline may never write it: an event handler (on*), style, srcdoc, an attribute this MJML component does not know, a value that would open a CSS declaration of its own (x;background:url(…)) or a URL with a refused scheme. The detail is the TAG and the ATTRIBUTE NAME, never the value (which may carry crafted markup).

members.name: ElementWrapped
members.description: A body- or section-level element was wrapped in a column to fit the model.

members.name: Empty
members.description: Input was empty.

members.name: IncludeUnresolved
members.description: An mj-include could not be resolved.

members.name: InputTooLarge
members.description: The input is larger than MaxInputBytes (UTF-8 bytes).

members.name: InvalidColor
members.description: A colour value on a block or container is not a CSS colour, so the message cannot carry it (it is written into a style). The message carries the PROPERTY name, never the value.

members.name: InvalidTableColor
members.description: A table cell's bgcolor was outside the colour allow-list (EmailColorPolicy) and was dropped from the model, because no message this pipeline renders could carry it.

members.name: NotMjml
members.description: The root element was not mjml.

members.description: The markup could not be parsed as XML.

items.description: An IStringLocalizer<TResourceSource> backed by JSON tables embedded in the resource type's assembly: {TResourceSource.FullName}.json for the neutral language and {TResourceSource.FullName}.{culture}.json per culture, each a flat { "Key": "Value" } map. The tables travel with the assembly and are never resolved through a host-supplied IStringLocalizerFactory, so an application that replaces the whole localization pipeline with its own factory still gets real text instead of raw key names; embedded JSON also resolves under Blazor WebAssembly, where resx satellite assemblies and the embedded neutral .resources are not loaded. Lookup walks CultureInfo.CurrentUICulture -> parent cultures -> neutral, each table is parsed at most once, and a missing table is an empty table rather than a failure. Register it as a CLOSED generic (IStringLocalizer<TMarker>) so it takes precedence over an open-generic registration, and pass a marker type that lives in the assembly holding the JSON files.

items.description: Structural edit operations over an EmailTemplateDocument: finding, adding, moving, removing and duplicating blocks, sections and columns. All operations work across nested hero/group/wrapper containers via DocumentTree.

members.name: AddBlock
members.description: Inserts a block into the column with the given id at index (clamped). Returns false if no such column exists.

members.name: AddColumn
members.description: Adds a column to the section and rebalances all columns to equal widths.

members.name: AddSection
members.description: Inserts a top-level section at index (clamped).

members.name: DuplicateBlock
members.description: Inserts a deep copy (with fresh ids) of the block immediately after the original, in the same container. Returns the copy, or null if the block was not found.

members.name: DuplicateSection
members.description: Inserts a deep copy (with fresh ids) of a top-level section immediately after the original. Returns the copy, or null if the section was not found.

members.name: FindBlock
members.description: Finds a block anywhere in the document by id, or returns null.

members.name: FindParentColumn
members.description: Returns the column that directly contains the given block, or null when the block is held by a non-column container (e.g. a hero) or does not exist.

members.name: MoveBlock
members.description: Moves a block to the target column at targetIndex (clamped, evaluated after removal). Returns false if the block or target column is missing.

members.name: MoveSection
members.description: Moves a top-level section to index (clamped after removal).

members.name: RebalanceColumns
members.description: Sets every column in the section to an equal share of the width (summing to 100%).

members.name: RemoveBlock
members.description: Removes a block from wherever it lives in the tree. Returns whether it was found.

members.name: RemoveColumn
members.description: Removes a column by id and rebalances the remaining columns. Returns whether found.

members.name: RemoveSection
members.description: Removes a top-level section by id. Returns whether it was found.

The BCL-only IHtmlContentSanitizer (D12/D22), the default whenever the Engine package is not registered — i.e. the editor in Blazor WebAssembly. A tokenizer with HTML-encode, never a regex strip: every <, >, &, " and ' is encoded by default, only HtmlSanitizerPolicy allow-listed tags are re-emitted (without attributes, exception a[href] after the scheme check), unclosed elements are completed and orphan closing tags are encoded, so content can never inject </mj-text>, <mj-raw> or <!--. Unknown or invalid input degrades to escaped text, never to passthrough, and the output may only be stricter than the AngleSharp implementation.

items.description: The colour allow-list of the model colours that reach the markup as an attribute (§3.7a): #rgb, #rrggbb and a named colour from a small fixed safe set. A value outside the list is dropped by the generator (with a warning), never sanitized into something else, because a CSS function or a quote would let a crafted string leave the attribute or fetch a remote resource.

members.name: IsAllowed
members.description: Answers whether a colour may be written into the markup. Empty is not a colour: the caller omits the attribute instead.

items.description: Validates a document against EmailImportOptions: the number of sections, the number of blocks and the block nesting depth. A host runs it on the server before saving (and the MJML importer uses the very same validator, so an import can never accept a document the save-time check rejects). Findings carry localization keys, never localized text.

members.name: Validate
members.description: Validates the document and returns every violated limit (empty when it fits).

members.name: Options
members.description: Gets the limits this validator applies.

items.description: Validates a document for structural and content correctness: layout (via LayoutValidator) plus per-block rules such as required button hrefs and image sources/alt text. Findings carry localization keys, never localized text.

members.name: MaxPreheaderLength
members.description: The longest preheader an inbox reliably shows before truncating it, measured in TEXT ELEMENTS (graphemes) of the SOURCE template — tokens included, because the inbox truncates the rendered text at the same visual width. A longer value is reported as a recommendation (Info), the single recommending rule of D9.

members.name: Validate
members.description: Validates the document and returns all findings (layout + block level).

items.description: One preview request: the document, the variable data as JSON, whether variables are substituted (false keeps the {{ }} tokens for an HTML export) and the culture the server should format values in. It travels outside the process untouched by design — the document is serialized with EmailTemplateSerializer, the rest are plain strings.

members.name: CultureName
members.description: Gets the culture name (for example cs-CZ); null = the renderer default (the document language, otherwise the invariant culture).

members.name: Document
members.description: Gets the document to render.

members.name: SubstituteVariables
members.description: Gets whether variables are substituted. false keeps the {{ … }} tokens in the output, which is what an HTML export with unresolved placeholders needs.

members.name: VariablesJson
members.description: Gets the variable data as JSON; null = renderer default sample data.

items.description: The rendered preview, or the reason it is missing. Html, Text and Subject are "" — never null — when the status is RenderFailed or Unavailable, so a host view never has to nil-check them. Warnings (a blocked URL, a removed event handler) keep the status Rendered: the HTML is complete.

members.name: Unavailable
members.description: A result that carries nothing because the renderer could not be reached — the HTML, text and subject are empty strings, never null.

members.name: Errors
members.description: Render diagnostics. Warnings (a blocked URL, a removed event handler) keep the status Rendered — the HTML is complete (D23).

members.name: Html
members.description: The rendered HTML, sandboxed by the caller (never trusted, see D17).

members.name: Preheader
members.description: The substituted preheader, when the document has one.

members.name: Status
members.description: Where the preview came from.

members.name: Subject
members.description: The substituted subject.

members.name: Text
members.description: The plain-text version.

items.description: Where the rendered preview came from: Rendered (possibly with warnings), RenderFailed (the template is at fault) or Unavailable (no registration, a network error or a server failure — retryable, not the author's bug).

The public read-only view of the pipeline's single URL allow-list (§3.7a, D15), for a UI that has to explain a rejected link before it reaches the markup. The list cannot be extended by a host: http, https, mailto, tel, a relative path without an authority and a #fragment pass; every other scheme and every network/UNC path is refused.

members.name: BlockedUrlPlaceholder
members.description: The value a refused URL is replaced with in the markup.

members.name: FindBlockedScheme
members.description: Returns the offending scheme (or the pseudo-scheme network-path) or null when the URL may be emitted.

members.name: IsAllowed
members.description: Answers whether a URL may be emitted into the message.

items.description: The single source of the HTML allow-lists both IHtmlContentSanitizer implementations read: which tags survive, which attributes may stay, which elements are dropped with their content and which are void. The link allow-list is the same URL scheme policy the render pipeline applies, so the two sanitizers can differ in strictness but never in what they allow.

members.name: IsHrefAllowed
members.description: Answers whether href may be emitted. The value is judged exactly as a browser would read it (character references decoded, tab/CR/LF removed), so javascript: is refused just like javascript:.

members.name: IsSafeStyle
members.description: Answers whether a style attribute value may be kept.

members.name: AllowedAttributes
members.description: Attributes the authoritative (AngleSharp) implementation may keep. The conservative implementation is stricter: it emits only ConservativeAttributes.

members.name: AllowedTags
members.description: Tags that may appear in sanitized inline HTML. Headings (h1–h6) are part of the set (D28): a mail author writes typography with them, and the WYSIWYG canvas has to show it. They are formatting elements exactly like b/i — the tag and its text survive, every attribute (style, on*, class) is dropped by both implementations.

members.name: ConservativeAttributes
members.description: Attributes the conservative implementation may emit — the single documented exception to "allow-listed tags are emitted without attributes" (D22): a[href] after the scheme check.

members.name: DroppedWithContent
members.description: Elements removed together with their content (they can execute or load).

members.name: VoidDroppedTags
members.description: Dropped elements that have no closing tag, so only the tag itself is removed instead of everything up to a closing tag that never comes.

members.name: VoidTags
members.description: Void elements of the allow-list: emitted without a closing tag.

items.description: Replaceable preview renderer: the one seam through which the editor gets a preview and an HTML export, so the render may run ON THE SERVER while the editor runs in Blazor WebAssembly without Scriban, Mjml.Net or AngleSharp. LocalEmailPreviewRenderer (Engine) is the default; a host that renders elsewhere registers its own. A missing registration is not a silent empty iframe — the editor shows Unavailable with a localized message naming the registration.
Renders an EmailTemplateDocument with a data model into HTML and text.

Sanitizes the inline HTML a text-bearing block may carry. Two implementations ship: ConservativeHtmlContentSanitizer in this package (pure BCL, the default when the Engine package is not registered) and AngleSharpHtmlContentSanitizer in Tempo.Blazor.EmailTemplates.Engine (authoritative parser, registered by AddTempoEmailTemplateEngine). Both read HtmlSanitizerPolicy and may only differ towards a stricter result.
Compiles MJML markup into responsive HTML.
The outcome of compiling MJML markup to HTML.

members.name: Errors
members.description: Any errors reported during compilation.

members.name: Html
members.description: The produced HTML (may be partial or empty when errors occurred).

members.name: Success
members.description: Gets whether compilation produced no errors.

items.description: Generates MJML markup from an EmailTemplateDocument. Default attribute values are omitted for clean output, attribute values are escaped, text-block HTML is sanitized, and a block's VisibleWhen wraps it in a Scriban condition.

members.name: Generate
members.description: Generates MJML for the document using the given options (render-safe by default).

items.description: Options controlling MJML generation.

members.name: Default
members.description: The default options (render-safe).

members.name: EmitHtmlAttributes
members.description: Gets or sets whether to emit mj-html-attributes. Off by default because the render engine (Mjml.Net) does not support it; turn on only when generating MJML for export so the markup round-trips losslessly.

members.name: ForExport
members.description: Options for producing MJML intended for export/round-trip (includes everything).

items.description: An error or warning produced while compiling MJML to HTML.

members.name: Column
members.description: 1-based source column, when known.

members.name: Key
members.description: Localization key of the diagnostic (for example BlockedUrlScheme), so a host can present a localized message; null for messages that come straight from the MJML compiler.

members.name: Line
members.description: 1-based source line, when known.

members.name: Message
members.description: Human-readable description of the problem (English fallback).

members.name: Severity
members.description: Whether the render failed (Error, the default) or completed with a security clean-up (Warning).

items.description: How serious a RenderError is. The numeric values are part of the public contract (D23) and must not be reordered — a host may persist or compare them.
Localization keys for diagnostics produced while rendering a template.

members.name: BlockedUrlScheme
members.description: A link, image or background used a URL scheme outside the allow-list and was replaced with # (§3.7a). Localized by the host; the resource entry lives in the editor package under the same key.

members.name: EventHandlerRemoved
members.description: Raw markup carried an event-handler attribute (on*) or srcdoc, which was removed because a variable inside it would run as script. The editor package carries the resource entry.

members.name: InvalidAttributeValue
members.description: An attribute value the message cannot carry was dropped from the generated markup: a value that would open a declaration of its own (x;background:url(…) in a padding, a colour or a font stack), which the MJML compiler copies verbatim into the element's inline style. The rest of the element renders normally. The attribute NAME is reported, never the value. The editor package carries the resource entry.

members.name: InvalidTableCellColor
members.description: A table cell carried a background colour outside the colour allow-list (#rgb, #rrggbb or a named colour of EmailColorPolicy), so the bgcolor attribute was omitted instead of being written. Severity is Warning: the rest of the message renders normally. The editor package carries the resource entry.

members.name: MarkupTooComplex
members.description: The rendered markup could not be checked within the guard's regex budget, so it was discarded and the render failed (Error): unchecked markup is never returned.

members.name: PreviewNotRegistered
members.description: No IEmailPreviewRenderer is registered, so there is nothing that could render a preview. The message names the missing registration (AddTempoEmailTemplateEngine() or a host IEmailPreviewRenderer).

members.name: PreviewUnavailable
members.description: The preview renderer itself could not produce a result (a server or transport failure). The editor shows this as Unavailable with a retry, not as a template error.

members.name: UnsafeElementRemoved
members.description: Markup that can rewrite a link at runtime was removed: an SVG animation element (set/animate/animateMotion/animateTransform/discard) or a meta http-equiv="refresh" redirect. E-mail has no legitimate use for either.

items.description: The fully rendered output of a template: substituted subject/preheader, HTML and text.

members.name: Errors
members.description: Errors and warnings gathered across the pipeline phases, in order.

members.name: HasWarnings
members.description: Gets whether the render produced any Warning.

members.name: Html
members.description: The rendered HTML body. Empty ("", never null) when the markup could not be built or could not be checked safely — an unchecked or half-compiled body is never handed to a host.

members.name: Preheader
members.description: The preheader after variable substitution, if any.

members.name: Subject
members.description: The subject after variable substitution.

members.name: Success
members.description: Gets whether rendering completed without errors. A Warning (a URL replaced with #, a removed event handler) does not fail the render — the message and its HTML are usable, so the host can still send it.

members.name: TextVersion
members.description: The plain-text alternative after variable substitution.

items.description: Per-render options handed to Render and RenderAsync. It is the extension point for render-scoped configuration (the culture of formatters); it deliberately has no escaping switch: the renderer decides the escaping mode per pass (§3.7, D14) and the only opt-out is the {{ value | html.trusted }} template filter. A host therefore cannot accidentally turn HTML escaping off.

members.name: Culture
members.description: Culture of the formatters (math.format, date.to_string, plain number output…). null means "decide from UseDocumentLanguageCulture": the culture of Language when that option is set, otherwise InvariantCulture — so a render never depends on the server's thread culture.

members.name: UseDocumentLanguageCulture
members.description: When true and Culture is null, the renderer takes the culture from the rendered document's language (an unknown language falls back to InvariantCulture). Render has no document, so the engine itself falls back to the invariant culture.

items.description: Produces the plain-text alternative of a document: HTML stripped, links rendered as text (url), sections separated by blank lines, tables row-by-row.

members.name: Generate
members.description: Generates the plain-text version of the document.

items.description: The shape of a validation rule's presentation keys: every rule key is one sentence, and the validation dialog shows it as a short title plus a description that says what it means and how to fix it. TitleOf/DescriptionOf build the two keys (for example validation.button.href_missing_Title and _Description) so a host never concatenates the suffix itself.

members.name: DescriptionSuffix
members.description: The suffix of a rule's description key: validation.button.href_missing_Description.

members.name: TitleSuffix
members.description: The suffix of a rule's title key: validation.button.href_missing_Title.

members.name: DescriptionOf
members.description: The description key of ruleKey: what the finding means and how to fix it.

members.name: TitleOf
members.description: The title key of ruleKey: a short name for the finding.

items.description: Marker type for the email template validation resources. Used with IStringLocalizer<EmailTemplateValidationResources> to resolve localized validation messages from the accompanying .resx files (neutral/English, Czech, French).
Thrown when an email template document cannot be (de)serialized — for example malformed JSON or an unknown block type discriminator. Carries a clear, surfaced message instead of crashing.

members.name: Key
members.description: Gets the localization key describing the failure, when it has one.

items.description: Serializes EmailTemplateDocument to and from JSON. Block polymorphism uses the type discriminator declared on EmailBlockBase. Unknown properties are ignored (forward compatibility); unknown block types and malformed JSON surface as EmailTemplateSerializationException.

members.name: CloneBlock
members.description: Creates an independent deep copy of a single block (same identifiers).

members.name: Deserialize
members.description: Deserializes a document from JSON, migrating it to CurrentSchemaVersion.

members.name: ReadSchemaVersion
members.description: Reads the schema version header of the JSON without deserializing the document (useful to decide about a migration or to build a friendly error). A missing (or non-positive) version means version 1.

members.name: Serialize
members.description: Serializes a document to a compact JSON string, always stamping the current schema version (SchemaVersion on the instance is never mutated).

members.name: SerializeContent
members.description: Serializes the CONTENT of a document: exactly Serialize without the UpdatedAt timestamp (a timestamp is bookkeeping, not content). The instance is never touched, not even temporarily, so it is safe to call on a document another component is reading. Two documents with equal signatures are the same template as far as saving is concerned.

members.name: Options
members.description: Gets the canonical serialization options used for documents, blocks and cloning.

items.description: Localization keys for template serialization diagnostics (never raw text).

members.name: InputTooLarge
members.description: The JSON is larger than MaxInputBytes (UTF-8 bytes).

members.name: InvalidSchemaVersion
members.description: The schema version header is missing a number, is not positive or appears twice.

members.name: Malformed
members.description: The JSON itself is malformed (not parseable, or an unsupported type).

members.name: TooDeeplyNested
members.description: The document nests blocks too deeply (or contains a block cycle) to be serialized.

members.name: UnsupportedSchemaVersion
members.description: The document uses a schema version newer than CurrentSchemaVersion.

items.description: Extracts every template variable referenced anywhere in a document — subject, preheader, block content and URLs, visibility conditions and raw block content — as a merged, de-duplicated set.

members.name: Extract
members.description: Returns the variables referenced across the whole document.

items.description: Renders, validates and analyzes Scriban-syntax templates within a sandbox.

Host-supplied template functions under one namespace. A provider lets an application add its own filters (for example currency formatting) without forking the engine: the functions are registered under Namespace and called from a template as {{ value | app.my_filter }}.

Optional audit sink for template sandbox events. Register zero to many implementations in DI; the engine resolves them as IEnumerable{T} and reports every refused member, namespace, function, URL scheme, limit and timeout. Audit is best effort: an exception thrown by a sink is swallowed and logged by the engine, never surfaced to the caller or the rendered output.

Validates template syntax without rendering — the only engine capability the editor's validation panel needs, so the editor no longer depends on ITemplateEngine. ScribanTemplateValidator (Engine) is the authoritative implementation; a host may register a server-side one; with nothing registered the panel shows a localized explanation that names the missing registration instead of pretending the template is fine.

Extracts the variable paths a template references. RegexTemplateVariableExtractor (BCL, this package) keeps the picker and sample data working without the Engine package; ScribanTemplateVariableExtractor (Engine) is the authoritative implementation. The difference is only how many variables are detected — never a security decision.

The BCL baseline ITemplateVariableExtractor: reads {{ path }}, {{ path.member }} and for … in <path> tokens without any Scriban dependency, so the variable picker and sample-data generator work in a WebAssembly editor that has no Engine package. A detection heuristic, not a parser — it under-reports rather than throwing.

members.name: Instance
members.description: The shared, stateless instance.

items.description: A success-or-error result that avoids throwing for expected failures.

members.name: Failure
members.description: Creates a failed result with an error message.

members.name: Success
members.description: Creates a successful result.

members.name: Error
members.description: Gets the error message (null when succeeded).

members.name: IsSuccess
members.description: Gets whether the operation succeeded.

members.name: Value
members.description: Gets the success value (default when failed).

items.description: Generates a plausible sample data model from a template's extracted variables, so previews and the "fill from template" action produce realistic, fully-populated output.

members.name: Generate
members.description: Builds a nested sample model (dictionaries/lists) covering all the given variables.

items.description: A single template syntax error with its source position.

members.name: Column
members.description: 1-based column number.

members.name: Line
members.description: 1-based line number.

members.name: Message
members.description: Human-readable description from the parser.

items.description: A function a provider exposes, for validation and docs.

One audit record emitted by a template render. Detail names the refused member, namespace, function or limit only — it never contains model values, so an audit trail cannot leak the data a template was rendering.

Classification of a TemplateSecurityEvent. The engine reports exactly these kinds and never invents new ones at runtime, so a host can switch on the enum exhaustively. The numeric values are part of the public contract (§3.6) and must not be reordered — a host may persist them.
Sandbox limits applied when rendering user-authored templates, bounding loops, recursion, output size and wall-clock time so a malicious or buggy template cannot hang or exhaust memory.

members.name: FunctionNamespaces
members.description: Namespaces of the registered ITemplateFunctionProviders (D6). The engine adds every provider namespace to its own copy, so a host-side template validator can tell a host function namespace (app.format_currency) from a data path and tolerate the unknown members of exactly these namespaces. It never widens the sandbox: the namespaces are validated when the engine is constructed and the member filter, the limits and the escaping keep applying.

members.name: LimitToString
members.description: Maximum length of a single string produced by converting a value to text, in UTF-16 characters (default 1,048,576). Exceeding it aborts the render instead of silently truncating.

members.name: LoopLimit
members.description: Maximum total loop iterations before rendering aborts (default 5000).

members.name: MaxOutputLength
members.description: Maximum length of the rendered output in characters (default 5,000,000).

members.name: ObjectRecursionLimit
members.description: Maximum recursion depth while converting an object graph to text (default 20), guarding deep or self-referencing values handed to the renderer as the model.

members.name: RecursiveLimit
members.description: Maximum recursion depth before rendering aborts (default 100).

members.name: RegexTimeOut
members.description: Timeout applied to every regular expression evaluated by the regex filters (default one second). Protects against catastrophic backtracking in a user-authored pattern. InfiniteMatchTimeout is rejected.

members.name: StrictVariables
members.description: When true, referencing an undefined variable is an error; otherwise it renders as empty (the default, lenient behaviour).

members.name: Timeout
members.description: Maximum wall-clock time for a single render (default 5 seconds, cooperative).

items.description: The result of validating a template's syntax.

members.name: SyntaxErrorKey
members.description: Localization key used for template syntax errors.

members.name: Invalid
members.description: Creates an invalid result with the given errors.

members.name: Errors
members.description: Gets the syntax errors found (empty when valid).

members.name: IsValid
members.description: Gets whether the template is syntactically valid.

members.name: Valid
members.description: A valid result.

items.description: A variable referenced by a template, with its dotted path and inferred kind.

members.name: Description
members.description: Gets the human-readable description shown next to the token in the variable picker (e.g. "First name of the user"). Supplied by the HOST: only the host knows what its data means. Variables extracted from a document leave it null, and the picker then shows the path alone. Participates in record equality (B9).

members.name: Group
members.description: Gets the optional group heading the picker sorts and labels rows under (e.g. "User", "Project"). Host-supplied; extracted variables leave it null and are listed ungrouped. Participates in record equality (B9).

members.name: Kind
members.description: Whether the variable is iterated as a collection.

members.name: Path
members.description: The dotted variable path (e.g. user.address.city).

items.description: Whether a template variable is used as a single value or iterated as a collection.
